summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: Under the 2020 Guardianship Act, when a parent revokes consent and the basis for a minor's guardianship no longer exists, Iowa Code section 232D.503(2) places the burden on the guardian to justify continuing it, and the constitutionally grounded parental preference survived the repeal of the old statutory preference; termination of the guardianship was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling Iowa authority on burden of proof and the parental preference in minor guardianship terminations under chapter 232D.
key_cases.quote: The constitutionally based parental preference predated section 633.559 and, in our view, survives its repeal.

key_cases.holding: An 'established' legal father who is neither the biological nor the adoptive father is not a 'parent' under chapter 232 and therefore is not a necessary party to CINA or termination proceedings; his remedy is to petition to intervene to seek guardianship or custody.
key_cases.relevance: Preserves a non-parent established father's route to guardianship or custody through post-termination intervention.
key_cases.quote: Daniel is neither J.C.'s biological father nor her adoptive father. Although Daniel is J.C.'s established father, he is not her parent under chapter 232.

key_cases.holding: Termination of a neglectful mother's rights to her ten-year-old son was affirmed; although Iowa prefers to keep siblings together and values family integrity, those preferences yield to clear and convincing evidence that the child's best interests require a permanent, stable adoptive home.
key_cases.relevance: Explains why continued placement with family cannot override a clear showing that permanency elsewhere serves the child.
key_cases.quote: However, this preference is not absolute. Our ultimate concern is the best interests of the child.

key_cases.holding: Reinstating the juvenile court's order terminating both parents' rights to a one-year-old under Iowa Code section 232.116(1)(h), the court found clear and convincing evidence the child could not be safely returned, held termination was in her best interests, and concluded that none of the permissive grounds in section 232.116(3) — including the relative-legal-custody exception in (3)(a) and the closeness-of-relationship exception in (3)(c) — applied.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that a child's placement with, and bond to, grandparents who are not her legal custodians does not trigger the section 232.116(3)(a) relative-custody exception, marking the limit of kinship-based arguments against termination.
key_cases.quote: A finding under subsection 3 allows the court not to terminate.
